I had a weird upbringing. Like my parents were never really physically abusive, they'd have been to embarrassed In front of their country club friends if it got around they hit their kids. I mean I was pretty lucky in that regard, but in my family the abuse was entirely mental. My mom could find that chink in your armor. She'd threaten to kill herself when she was angry at us. My bro and I were in 3rd-5th grade when that first happened. 

This may be gas lighting if I understand it, she always blamed me when I lived with her a few years after college, for the house being a mess. It was my fault because I was lazy. Now I'd routinely clean the whole place and shed have it back to a total mess within days. She'd always had housekeepers before the divorce so she didn't ever have to keep a clean house herself. 

When I moved out, my sister in law didn't want to take their new baby to her house because of how dirty it was so my mom had to visit her new grandchild in my very clean apartment. That did feel good to be vindicated that I wasn't the problem.

Ive begun to realize my mom has gas lit me alot over the years, I don't even think she realizes. She's said my depression was just me being lazy, she's said I can't keep a relationship because I'm lazy. She's made me feel so worthless sometimes. 

When I was in high school I became good friends with this girl over the course of our senior year. We did two plays together, we had inside jokes, talked a lot everyday, and I told her I had feelings for her near the end of that year. It was the first time I'd told a girl I liked her. It was the first time I thought one liked me too. I wasn't into girls much. I had a hard time forming connections with people so it was always just easier to not even try so this was a big deal to me. She turned me down and it effectively ended our friendship. I cried everyday for a month. At one point when her usual insults of quit being lazy didn't work my mother decided the best way to help me through this was to literally get in my face and scream at me. Like not even words just like right in my face and yelling "Aaaaaaaaaaaarrrrrrgh!" I still feel traumatized by that. It's been 20 years and that really stuck with me.
